options: It always points to exactly one object type, like a standard lookup
It can point to more than one kind of object depending on the record, e.g. Task/Event's WhatId

questions.q: Why does SELECT What.Phone FROM Event fail without TYPEOF?
options: What.Phone requires a semi-join to resolve
Phone is not a valid field on any object Event can relate to
Event does not support relationship queries at all
SOQL doesn't know in advance which object type's fields it should look up, since What can point to several different types
questions.explain: Because What is polymorphic, SOQL can't resolve a plain field reference against it without TYPEOF explicitly branching on the resolved type.

questions.q: In a TYPEOF query, what does the ELSE branch do?
options: Specifies fallback fields for any resolved type not explicitly handled by a WHEN branch
Is required syntax and causes an error if omitted
Filters out records of unhandled types entirely
Only applies to custom polymorphic fields, never standard ones
questions.explain: ELSE is optional, providing fallback fields for any type not matched by an explicit WHEN — omitting it just means those rows won't have those extra fields populated.

questions.q: When is filtering with WHERE What.Type IN ('Account', 'Opportunity') preferable to writing a full TYPEOF clause?
options: Only when querying custom objects, never standard objects
When you need completely different fields returned depending on the record's type
When you only need to filter which records come back by type, without needing different fields per type
Never — TYPEOF should always be used instead
questions.explain: The Type qualifier is a lighter-weight option for simple type-based filtering; TYPEOF is for when the selected fields themselves need to differ by type.

questions.q: In Apex, how can you check a specific queried record's resolved polymorphic type at runtime?
options: Using a semi-join inside Apex
Using the instanceof operator, e.g. if (e.What instanceof Account)
By calling TYPEOF() as an Apex method
Polymorphic type cannot be checked in Apex, only in SOQL
questions.explain: instanceof lets Apex code check a polymorphic field's actual resolved type after the records have been queried.
